Created the Millennium Challenge Corporation, a small government corporation that gives large, multi-year grants to poor countries that pass a scorecard of governance, economic freedom, and social investment indicators. It was enacted as Title VI of Division D of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2004.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Enacted text: Pub. L. 108-199](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/plaw/108/public/199){.btn-official} [Current U.S. Code: 22 U.S.C. 7701 et seq.](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/22/7701?link-type=html){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Eligibility determined by a board using published third-party indicators.
- Compacts of up to five years negotiated with and implemented by the partner country.
- Threshold programs for countries that fall just short of eligibility.

## Why it matters

It was designed as an alternative to the model in the [Foreign Assistance Act](faa-1961.qmd): selective, country-led, and insulated from short-term foreign policy uses of aid. It is the standard example in debates about aid selectivity.

## Current status

In force. The Millennium Challenge Corporation was targeted for deep cuts in 2025. Check current status of the agency and its compacts.

[Last checked November 10, 2026.]{.checked}
